Steak Summer Rolls

On October 29, 2026October 29, 2026
by chanie
in Appetizer, Meat & Poultry, Recipes, Shabbos
Leave a Comment on Steak Summer Rolls

I don’t know if I’m more excited for you to have this recipe, or to share the cookbook that it’s from! My friend Miriam Pascal, of Overtimecook as well as the author of one of my favorite dessert cookbooks, Something Sweet, is releasing her latest cookbook in the “Real Life” series, Real Life Shabbos Cooking.

Now let me tell you something about Miriams Shabbos food – I’ve experienced it – in real life. I was lucky enough to be her Shabbos guest at her home in California, not once, but twice! I still dream about her focaccia challah (yes, the recipe is in the book), all her delicious dips, dumplings, and so much more.

Aside from her delicious food, Miriam and I both have a passion (read: obsession) for good coffee, and her coffee bar is a dream, complete with an incredible coffee machine and the best ice nuggets. She also always has delicious cookies and cakes to eat along with it.

With the book release next week, I invited Miriam over to cook something together from the book, and the summer rolls were right up my alley! We had so much fun making them together! I’ve always struggled working with rice paper, and Miriam taught me a few tricks that really helped. I was so excited to make her a cup of coffee for a change, and I took out my Cumulus machine for an iced nitro cold brew which we thoroughly enjoyed before the fleish.

I’m so excited for you to have Miriam’s incredible Shabbos recipes in your hands, she really thought of everything in the book from Shabbos kiddush to shalosh seudot and everything in between!

Steak Summer Rolls
YIELD 12-15 rolls

1 (approx. 2-lb) London broil OR flank steak, thinly sliced
¼ cup soy sauce, GF soy sauce, tamari sauce, OR coconut aminos
½ cup pineapple juice
2 cubes frozen garlic
2 cubes frozen ginger
¼ cup brown sugar,
1 teaspoon kosher salt

MISO PEANUT DIPPING SAUCE
⅓ cup creamy peanut butter
1 Tablespoon white miso paste
¼ cup soy sauce, GF soy sauce, tamari sauce, OR coconut aminos
1 Tablespoon toasted sesame oil
¼ cup pineapple juice
2 Tablespoons honey

ASSEMBLY
12-15 rice papers
green or red cabbage, shredded
carrots, shredded
sugar snap peas, halved
bell pepper, sliced
scallions, sliced
avocado, sliced
cucumber, sliced
sesame seeds, optional, for garnish

Prepare the steak: Combine all marinade ingredients in a ziplock bag. Add sliced steak; seal and marinate for 1 hour,
up to overnight.

Heat a large frying pan over high heat. Add steak and marinade; cook, stirring occasionally, for 5-8 minutes, or until
steak reaches desired level of doneness. Discard liquid; set meat aside.

Prepare the miso peanut dipping sauce: Place all dipping sauce ingredients into a container; use an immersion
blender to combine until smooth and creamy. (This can also be done in a blender or food processor.)

Assemble the summer rolls: Fill a deep plate with water. Submerge 1 sheet of rice paper for 15-20 seconds, until just
a bit softened but not too soft. Place rice paper on a flat surface.

Add steak and vegetables of choice in a line in the center. Fold eggroll style: Fold sides over the filling, then roll to
fully encase in rice paper. Set aside. Repeat with remaining rice paper, steak, and vegetables.

Serve summer rolls on a platter, alongside a bowl of dipping sauce. If desired, sprinkle sesame seeds over summer
rolls.

PLAN AHEAD
Summer rolls can be prepared 1-2 days in advance. Wrap them in parchment paper to prevent them from drying out; refrigerate, covered.
